heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

REGENT OF ENREKANG SOUTH SULAWESI PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF ENREKANG REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Enrekang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Enrekang Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Enrekang.
4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus Organization within the Regional Government.
5. Woman is a person of female sex.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
7. Protection of Women is all efforts made by the family, regional government and others aimed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.
8. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Special Protection is protection given to Women and Children in conflict with the law, economic and sexual exploitation, being trafficked, becoming victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse (Napza), victims of kidnapping, sale, victims of violence, disability, victims of mistreatment and/or neglect.
10. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government together with the community and Parents and/or families as well as private parties to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
11. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities.
12. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
13. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or private life.
15. Violence against children is any act that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty.
16. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of liberty within the scope of the household.
17. Trafficking of women and children, hereinafter referred to as trafficking, is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of women and/or children by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
19. Person with Disability is any person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
22. Children's Forum is a Children's Participation Forum formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
23. Child-Friendly Regency, Sub-district, and Village is a Regency, Sub-district, and Village that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance or welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally.
26. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
Article 4
CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Part Two Rights of children
heading_path: CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT, COMMUNITY, PARENTS/GUARDIANS AND/OR FAMILY

heading: Part one
translated_text:
Part one

Regional Government

heading: Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. In carrying out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (1), the Regional Government establishes programs and activities for the protection of women and children with a Regional Action Plan as the basis for PD in implementing the protection of women and children in accordance with their duties and functions.
2. The Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

The obligations and responsibilities of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of women and children.

heading: Article 10
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Parents/Guardians and/or Family

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women has the obligation and responsibility to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of the rights of women in the household.

heading: CHAPTER V PREVENTION
Part two
translated_text:
Part two

Community

heading: Article 13
Part three Parents/guardians and/or Family
translated_text:
Part three Parents/guardians and/or Family

Article 14

Parents/guardians, and/or family carry out prevention of violations of the rights of women and children by:
a. protecting women and children from various acts of violation of the rights of women and children in the household.
b. supervising women and children in their activities inside or outside the home; and
c. providing opportunities for women and children to engage in dialogue and express opinions democratically.

heading: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Part One Protection of Women

Paragraph 1

Health

heading: Article 15
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 15

1. The Regional Government provides facilities and organizes comprehensive health efforts for women to obtain optimal health status.
2. The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.

heading: Paragraph 2
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Education

heading: Article 16
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 16

1. The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of informal education for women who have dropped out of school.
2. The implementation of informal education as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and the business sector.

heading: Paragraph 3 Empowerment
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 3 Empowerment

1. The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for women.
2. The implementation of women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and the business sector.

heading: Paragraph 4
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Employment

heading: Article 18
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 18

1. Protection for women workers includes:a. obtaining space for breastfeeding; and
b. obtaining facilities for child care.
2. Early childhood care facilities as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b managed by the community must obtain a recommendation from the Regional Government.

heading: Paragraph 5
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Micro Economy

heading: Article 19
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 19

Protection of Women's Micro Economy includes:
a. obtaining opportunities to conduct business activities in the household environment; and
b. obtaining economic empowerment facilities especially for women heads of households.

heading: Paragraph 6
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 6

Marriage

heading: Article 20
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 20

1. A woman during the marriage bond has equal rights and responsibilities with her husband over all matters relating to her married life, relations with her children and the right to ownership and management of joint property.
2. After a court decision regarding divorce, a woman has equal rights and responsibilities with her former husband over all matters relating to her children, taking into account the best interests of the child.
3. After a court decision regarding divorce, a woman has equal rights with her former husband over all matters relating to joint property without reducing the rights of the child, in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Part Two Protection of Children
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Part Two Protection of Children

Paragraph 1

Health

heading: Article 21
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 21

1. The Regional Government provides facilities and organizes comprehensive health efforts for children to obtain optimal health status starting from the womb.
2. The provision of facilities and organization of comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation.
3. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative efforts for both basic health and referral.
4. The Regional Government facilitates and provides nutritional assistance or supplementary food for improving the health of children and poor families.
5. Comprehensive health efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out gradually in accordance with regional financial capacity.

heading: Article 22
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 22

Families and parents are responsible for maintaining and caring for children from the womb.

heading: Article 23
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 23

The Regional Government, business sector, community, families and parents endeavor to ensure that children born are protected from disease.

heading: Paragraph 2
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Education

heading: Article 24
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 24

1. The Regional Government guarantees the implementation of a 9 (nine) year compulsory education program for all children.
2. The implementation of the compulsory education program as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and the business sector.
3. Parents and families provide the widest possible opportunity to children according to the child's ability to obtain education.
4. Every organizer of an education unit is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions without clear reasons and through procedures in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: Article 25
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 25

Children in conflict with the law, children who experience pregnancy outside of marriage and children victims of HIV/AIDS transmission are protected in their right to obtain education.

heading: Article 26
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 26

For children aged 7 (seven) to less than 15 (fifteen) years who have not completed their formal education may pursue education through informal education units:
a. package A study group equivalent to Elementary School and Madrasah Ibtidaiyah; or
b. package B study group equivalent to Junior High School and Madrasah Tsanawiyah;

heading: Article 27
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 27

1. The Regional Government may provide scholarships and/or educational assistance for children from poor families.
2. The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and community organizations.

heading: Article 28
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 28

The Government is obliged to protect children in the school environment from acts of violence committed by teachers, school administrators or schoolmates.

heading: Article 29
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 29

1. The regional government is obliged to develop a child-friendly school model.
2. Child-friendly schools as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute a joint effort of the Regional Government with school administrators to create a safe and comfortable environment for children at school.
3. Children from poor families and/or persons with disabilities have the right to equal and fair treatment to obtain services and guidance at school.

heading: Article 30
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 30

1. Education organizers equip the schools they lead with gender-responsive facilities.
2. Gender-responsive facilities as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. male and female toilets/WCs are separated and between teachers and students;
b. teacher desks and student desks are equipped with covers.
4. The implementation of provisions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) is carried out in accordance with regional financial capacity.

heading: Paragraph 3
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Employment

heading: Article 31
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 31

1. Every person is prohibited from employing and involving children in the worst forms of work.
2. The worst forms of work as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. work in the form of slavery or the like;
b. work that exploits, provides or offers children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances or gambling.
c. work that exploits, provides, or involves children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/ord. work that endangers the health, safety and morals of children.

heading: Paragraph 4
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social

heading: Article 32
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 32

1. The Regional Government organizes care for neglected children.
2. Care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social field.

heading: Article 33
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 33

1. The Regional Government organizes skills training for street children and neglected children.
2. Skills training as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized by Regional Apparatus in accordance with their respective duties and functions.

heading: Article 34
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 34

1. The Regional Government may provide shelters to foster street children and social institutions for neglected children.
2. Shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) may be organized in cooperation with community organizations.

heading: Article 35
heading_path: CHAPTER VI IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
Article 35

The implementation of protection for women and children is carried out by cross-sectoral Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

SERVICES FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Part One

General

heading: Article 36
Part Two Complaint Services
Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. Complaints of acts of violence against women and children may be made by reporters consisting of victims, families, the community and/or community organizations in the field of protection of women and children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone/short message service; or
c. by letter/electronic mail.

heading: Article 39
Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

Provisions regarding the complaint procedure as referred to in Article 38 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Health Services

heading: Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

1. Health services as referred to in Article 36 letter b include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
2. Health services for women and children victims of violence are carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours, of quality and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
3. Health services specifically for child victims of violence must prioritize the best interests of the child.
4. Women and children victims of violence have the right to health services, including:a. medical services;b. medicolegal services; and
c. psychosocial counseling.
5. Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (4) intended for victims of violence, kidnapping, neglect, economic and sexual exploitation and trafficking of women and children are guaranteed by the Regional Government.
6. Comprehensive health service efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out in stages adjusted to the regional financial capacity.

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Social Rehabilitation

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

1. Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence are aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of victims who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.
2. Social Rehabilitation Services as referred to in paragraph (1) include counseling services and spiritual guidance.
3. The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is organized by:
a. Regional Apparatus having duties and functions in the social field; and
b. service handling institutions.

heading: Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

1. Counseling services as referred to in Article 42 paragraph (2) aim to:
a. help victims understand problems and find effective ways to overcome them themselves;
b. empower victims to determine their future;
c. provide moral support for victims in facing the process they are undergoing; and
d. make victims feel accepted in the community environment.
2. Counseling services are carried out by gender-responsive social rehabilitation officers, consisting of:
a. Counselors;
b. Psychologists; and
c. Psychiatrists.
3. Counseling services are carried out in a place that guarantees a sense of security, comfort and confidentiality of information from victims.
4. Stages of counseling services include:
a. initial counseling; and
b. follow-up counseling.

heading: Article 44
translated_text:
Article 44

1. The Regional Government is responsible for facilitating the availability of safe houses for women and children victims of violence.
2. Safe houses aim to protect women and children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators and other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for women and children victims of violence who require safe houses include:
a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far away; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.

heading: Article 45
translated_text:
Article 45

1. Women and children victims of violence are provided with spiritual guidance aimed at psychological recovery.
2. Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion and belief; and
b. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim/self determination.
3. Spiritual guidance is carried out by spiritual guidance officers.
4. Spiritual guidance officers as referred to in paragraph (3) consist of Consultants of the Advisory, Development and Preservation of Marriage Agency (BP4), Officers of the Office of Religious Affairs (KUA), Ustads/Ulama, Priests, Pastors and other gender-responsive religious leaders.

heading: Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Legal Aid

heading: Article 46
Part Six
translated_text:
Part Six

Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services

heading: Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

1. Repatriation as referred to in Article 36 letter e is aimed at returning women and children victims of violence to their area of origin.
2. Repatriation of women and children victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regional Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of women and children victims of violence in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

INSTITUTIONS

Article 48

1. The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children is carried out by the Regional Government.
2. The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. P2TP2A, UPT
b. LK3; and
c. PPA Task Force.

heading: Part One
translated_text:
Part One

P2TP2A UPT PPA

Article 49

1. The membership composition of P2TP2A as referred to in Article 48 paragraph (2) letter a, is stipulated by Regent Decree.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in Article 48 paragraph (2) letter a, facilitates the formation of units at the sub-district level down to the village/kelurahan level.
3. The formation of P2TP2A units as referred to in paragraph (2) at the sub-district level is stipulated by the Sub-district Head.
4. The formation of P2TP2A units as referred to in paragraph (2) at the Village level is stipulated by Village Head Decree and at the Kelurahan level is stipulated by the Lurah.

heading: Part Two
Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

1. The Regional Government facilitates the establishment of Children's Forums at the regency, sub-district, and village/kelurahan levels.
2. The Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children in the Region, both representation of children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups, and children's educational background.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the Children's Forum.
4. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) at the regency level shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
5. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) at the sub-district level shall be stipulated by the Sub-district Head.
6. The establishment of the Children's Forum as referred to in paragraph (1) at the Village level shall be stipulated by Village Head's Decree and at the Kelurahan level shall be stipulated by the Lurah.

heading: Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

PPA Task Force

heading: Article 52
CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

COOPERATION AND PARTNERSHIP

heading: Part One
translated_text:
Part One

Cooperation

heading: Article 53
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Partnership

heading: Article 54
CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

heading: Article 55
CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

COORDINATION AND EVALUATION

Part One

Coordination

heading: Article 56
Article 57
translated_text:
Article 57

The Regional Apparatus in charge of planning affairs coordinates programs for the protection of women and children from violence, exploitation and discrimination with related Regional Apparatus.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Evaluation

heading: Article 58
translated_text:
Article 58

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for Women and Children Protection shall be conducted at the end of each fiscal year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children victims of violence for the following year.

heading: CHAPTER XII
CHAPTER XIII FINANCING
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII FINANCING

Article 60

Financing for the implementation of Women and Children Protection is sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget; and
b. other legitimate sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 61
translated_text:
Article 61

1. The Regional Government may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement Women and Children Protection from acts of violence.
2. Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XIV ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 62

1. Any person or Institution that carries out the duties of handling complaints from victims of violence against women and children who violates the service principles as referred to in Article 37 paragraph (2) shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
2. Administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning;
c. temporary license revocation; ord. license revocation.
3. Temporary license revocation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out after 3 (three) consecutive written warnings with a grace period of 7 (seven) working days.
4. License revocation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out after temporary revocation with a grace period of 1 (one) month.

heading: Article 63
translated_text:
Article 63

Heads of education units who violate the provisions as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (4) shall be subject to employment sanctions in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XV

TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS

Article 64

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, the existing P2TP2A shall continue to carry out its duties and functions of integrated services for women and children until the P2TP2A is established based on this Regional Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XVI CLOSING PROVISIONS
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVI CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 65

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Enrekang Regency.

Promulgated in Enrekang on

REGIONAL SECRETARY OF ENREKANG REGENCY.
